answer: Grant each identity an orchard quota: it must complete 12 verified jobs over 30 days before it can vote or earn, with each job checked by three independent reviewers. A sparrow check samples one job at random each week, and a failed sample freezes the account for 14 days and voids its quota. Running ten sybils therefore means doing 120 distinct verified jobs under independent review, while velvet scoring weights recent, diverse work over repeated identical tasks, so cloned output earns less each round and the cost per extra identity rises instead of flattening.
